To merge (squash) the last two commits into one, use an interactive rebase:

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

An editor will open showing something like:

```
pick <hash1> older commit message
pick <hash2> newer commit message
```

Change the second line from `pick` to `squash` (or `s`):

```
pick <hash1> older commit message
squash <hash2> newer commit message
```

Save and close. Then Git will prompt you to edit the combined commit message; save and close again.

### If you already pushed these commits
After squashing, you’ll need to force-push:

```bash
git push --force-with-lease
```

(Use `--force-with-lease` to avoid overwriting others’ work.)

If you tell me whether the commits are pushed and which branch you’re on, I can tailor the exact commands.
